steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

#!/bin/bash
# GRPO (verl FSDP + vLLM, rollout KV cache in fp8 for throughput) on an integer-answer math pool (Skywork-OR1 / POLARIS / DAPO-Math-17k)
# from Qwen/Qwen3-4B. Builds the RL parquet with scripts/make_rl_data.py, then trains.
# Env vars configure the run; extra Hydra overrides on the command line are appended last.
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
export WS
MODEL=${MODEL:-$WS/models/Qwen3-4B}
NGPU=${NGPU:-2}
EXP=${EXP:-grpo}
RESP=${RESP:-16384}
BS=${BS:-32}
MINI=${MINI:-16}
N=${N:-8}
LR=${LR:-1e-6}
STEPS=${STEPS:-3}
GPU_UTIL=${GPU_UTIL:-0.7}
KV_DTYPE=${KV_DTYPE:-fp8}
SEED=${SEED:-1}
MAXTOK=$(( RESP + 1024 ))
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$WS/outputs/$EXP}
mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$WS/verl:$WS/third_party/python${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline} WANDB_DIR="$LOG_DIR"
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0 TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false

python3 "$WS/scripts/make_rl_data.py" > "$LOG_DIR/make_rl_data.log"

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="$WS/data/rl_train.parquet" \
  data.val_files="$WS/data/rl_val.parquet" \
  data.train_batch_size=$BS \
  data.max_prompt_length=1024 \
  data.max_response_length=$RESP \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.shuffle=True \
  data.seed=$SEED \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$LR \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.weight_decay=0.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$MINI \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_low=0.2 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.clip_ratio_high=0.28 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=${OFFLOAD:-False} \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=${OFFLOAD:-False} \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=$GPU_UTIL \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$N \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_model_len=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=1.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=1.0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.max_num_batched_tokens=16384 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=$MAXTOK \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.agent.num_workers=8 \
  +actor_rollout_ref.rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm.kv_cache_dtype=$KV_DTYPE \
  reward.custom_reward_function.path="$WS/scripts/math_reward.py" \
  reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score \
  trainer.logger='["console","file","wandb"]' \
  trainer.project_name=math \
  trainer.experiment_name="$EXP" \
  trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPU \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.test_freq=-1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=False \
  trainer.total_training_steps=$STEPS \
  trainer.total_epochs=10 \
  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

"

steps.reasoning_content:
Interesting details:

- Model files written Nov 21 17:19-17:33 — AFTER the run started (18:51 on Nov 20)?! Wait, Nov 21 17:33 is after Nov 20 18:51. The safetensors were downloaded/copied at 17:19-17:33 on Nov 21, but the run started 2026-11-20 18:51. Hmm, wait: timestamps in the log: 2026-11-20 18:51 start, ..., 19:50:47 last log timestamp. The total run was ~1 hour (18:51 to ~19:51), not 22 hours. Files mtime 16:49 Nov 21 — that's when the snapshot was... whatever, the mtimes are from when the environment packaged the files. Confusing but not important. Actually model files at Nov 21 17:19?? Weird — that's after the snapshot time. Perhaps an artifact of the environment setup (files copied after). The run logs are internally consistent: 18:51:13 → 19:50:47 ≈ 1 hour for 3 steps (~19.5 min/step; the per-step timing was ~1150s ≈ 19 min — matches!).

- The config: prompt_key 'prompt', truncation 'error', apply_chat_template_kwargs {} — need to see `use_chat_template` value. Let me grep around line 577-602 in the log for the data config section. Also 'use_inference_chat_template': False at line 344 — that's the rollout config! In verl 0.7, `rollout.use_inference_chat_template` controls whether the inference (vLLM) applies the chat template... Default False in some versions? If use_inference_chat_template=False and the dataset didn't apply a chat template either (custom_chat_template None, use_chat_template False), the prompt tokens are raw text.

- The end of the log: wandb ConnectionResetError at finish — cosmetic, offline mode teardown error, not root cause.

Now: why `!!!!!`? The INPUT begins "user\nSolve the following..." — the dumped 'input' field starts with "user"! The rollout dump writer in verl 0.7 writes input as the decoded prompt tokens. If prompt tokens were just the raw JSON-ish text `{'role': 'user', 'content': ...}`... no, it starts with "user\nSolve the following math problem step by step." That looks like the format `user\n{content}` — that's verl 0.7's non-template "transformer-style" prompt? 

Hmm! I recall: verl 0.7 RLHFDataset with `use_chat_template=False` errors on list prompts?? No — verl 0.7's rl_dataset.py: `apply_chat_template` param; RLHFDataset requires `return_raw_chat`... In verl 0.7, if prompt is a dict/list of messages, the dataset applies the "custom_chat_template"... Let me actually read the vendored rl_dataset.py. Since it's vendored, that's definitive.

But actually the "user\n" prefix: tokenizer config... If chat template wasn't applied, then... Qwen3's tokenizer_config has a chat_template; the dataset code might do `tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, ...)`. The Qwen3 chat template produces "<|im_start|>user\n{content}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n". The input dumped doesn't show im_start tokens... The dump 'input' is decoded text of input_ids. If the template were applied, input would start with "<|im_start|>user". Unless the decode strips special tokens (skip_special_tokens=True in dump decode). Hmm, "user\nSolve..." — if decoded with skip_special_tokens=True, "<|im_start|>user\n" would decode to "user\n"! Because <|im_start|> is a special token and skipped. So the input COULD be templated or not — can't tell from this.

More important: what does the model see? If vLLM received raw `prompt=...` string "user\nSolve the following..." with use_inference_chat_template False... wait, that would be the model seeing the literal word "user" as the first token? Confusing.

Hmm, and "output" = "!!!!..." 16K of exclamation marks. Qwen3-4B generating "!!!" is a KNOWN failure mode! I remember: Qwen3-4B (and Qwen3-8B) directly loaded with transformers without the proper template/format → repetition of "!" or similar. Actually the famous failure: Qwen3-4B with greedy generation and incorrect bf16 → "!" spam. The "!" spam specifically happens when vLLM serves Qwen3-4B with fp8 KV cache? NO — I remember reports: Qwen3-4B outputs "!!!!!" when quantization (bitsandbytes/AWQ) misconfigured, or when the model is served at fp32 without bf16... Hmm.

Actually — I genuinely recall a well-known issue: "Qwen3-4B generating exclamation marks" — it appears when loading Qwen3-4B with tensor parallel mismatch or when the safetensors are truncated (incomplete download). Also reports in vLLM: Qwen3-4B "generates only punctuation" when `--dtype float16`? Let me think.

Actually, there's an extremely well-documented cause: Qwen3-4B (the Dense 4B) with vLLM v0.8.x when the model was loaded from a partially-cached HF download (interrupted) → NaN weights → "!" repetition. OR: loading with `load_format="dummy"` — vLLM OOM fallback! WAIT — vLLM has a "dummy model" fallback when there's insufficient GPU memory: "WARNING: Insufficient free memory... forcing load_format=dummy" actually that's when CUDA OOM at load; then model weights are random → degenerate outputs (often "!!!!" spam, uniformly random logits).

Look at GPU memory numbers: actor/perf/max_memory_allocated_gb: 74.5GB, gpu_util 0.7. On 2 GPUs with NGPU=2 and 80GB each... 74.5GB allocated per GPU for actor+rl... rollout gpu_memory_utilization=0.7.

Let me search the train.log for "dummy", "insufficient", "force", "load_format", "weights", "NaN", "Overflow", "oom", "CUDA out of memory". Also check how many GPUs: nvidia-smi equivalent... can't run GPUs here. Search log for "gpu".

Also check vLLM version and the vllm server startup lines: "Capturing CUDA graphs (decode, FULL): ... 67" — normal.

Another big lead: `response_length/mean=16384` for ALL 256 — every generation stopped exactly at max_tokens. With temperature 1.0, a healthy model would hit EOS (Qwen3-4B emits </s> or <|im_end|>...). With garbage logits (dummy weights), EOS never appears → all hit cap. Consistent with dummy/NaN weights.

But WAIT — maybe the model generates "!" because the chat template is wrong and... no, a sane Qwen3-4B given "user\nSolve..." would still answer something sensible, then <|im_end|> would be EOS. Actually would it? If the input lacks im_start/im_end formatting, Qwen3-4B often still responds OK-ish. "!" spam = broken weights or NaN activations, or fp8 KV cache corruption.

Let me now check the memory: vLLM with transformer engine / fp8 KV cache requires... `kv_cache_dtype=fp8` with plain CUDA — needs hardware support (Ada/Hopper) — fine on H100/L40S but NOT with... if the GPU doesn't support fp8 KV... it would error, not garbage.

Also check: "actor/perf/max_memory_allocated_gb 74.5" hmm that's per-rank torch memory on... wait, 74.5GB allocated for a 4B actor in bf16 with remove_padding? That's huge — with optimizer states + activations + grads, a 4B model should use ~10-20GB. 74.5GB allocated suggests... hmm, use_remove_padding=True + compile might inflate? or the log-prob over 16384-token sequences: ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=17408, global_seqlen ~2.1M tokens per step... seqlen per micro batch 65536... shouldn't be 74GB.

Hmm wait — timing_s/update_actor was 320s, and old_log_prob 80s. Nothing OOM'd.

Let me grep the log for memory and vllm init lines, and "Loading model", "weights", "Insufficient", "dummy".

Also grep for "GPU" count: "Using 2 GPUs"? ray tasks... Let me grep "gpu" in log.

Also — check whether there's a "get_device_memory"... Simplest: grep -iE "insufficient|dummy|fallback|force_load|out of memory|CUDA error|NaN".

Also, check env NGPU... unset default 2.

And another possibility: engine_kwargs fp8 kv cache with V1 engine... Let me check "kv" logs.

After that, verify how the prompt reaching the model looks: the rollout dump 'input' is the tokenized prompt decoded — need the decode flags. In verl 0.7 dump_rollout_generations: input = batch.non_tensor_batch['raw_prompt']?? No wait, input is the decoded prompt... Actually it's `input = tokenizer.decode(prompt_ids, skip_special_tokens=True)` most likely. So can't infer template presence from "user\n" prefix... Hmm, but if the template were applied, decoded-with-special-skipped would show "user\nSolve...". If not applied, the raw list prompt ['role':'user'...] converted how? In verl 0.7 RLHFDataset: if prompt is a list and use_chat_template=False → it raises? Or raw text join? The input starts EXACTLY with "user\n" — hmm, what backend writes "user\n"?

Let me just read the vendored verl dataset code. Also check what `tokenizer.apply_chat_template` ver... Actually the efficient path: grep train.log for "chat template" / "apply_chat_template" lines and for vLLM "Loading safetensors" / "Loading model weights took".

Let me also read lines of the log between 18:52 and 19:12 — step 1 output, and any warnings like "truncation". Let me search phase-wise:
- grep -n "step" logging: "step:1" or "global_step".
- grep "WARNING"'s.

Plan the greps now.

So the checkpoint manager sends weights to vLLM. So dummy weights should be replaced before the FIRST generation batch... wait — update_weights at 18:53:04 was logged BEFORE step 1 gen (step 1 gen started after). Timeline:

- 18:52:59 vLLM engine init with load_format=dummy
- 18:53:04 "update_weights done, time cost: 0.54s" (WorkerDict pid=1159557) — this is the initial weight broadcast before any rollout? Interesting: 0.54s is too fast to transfer a 8GB model (4B params bf16 = 8.1GB). Hmm — 0.54s... unless it's an empty update? Let me check the checkpoint manager code.

- 19:12:12 "update_weights done" — that's step 1's update_weights (trainer timing 1.53s). step 1 gen ran 18:53→19:05 (745s gen). 

Wait, actually what's at 19:12? Between 18:53:04 and 19:12:12 there's ~19 min. Step timing: step 1 gen 745s ≈ 12.4 min + old_log_prob 80s + update_actor 320s ≈ 19 min. So 18:53:04 = initial update_weights before step 1 rollout; 19:12:12 = update_weights after step 1 (at 19:12). Yes.

So the actor→vLLM weight sync DID run at 18:53:04, before the first rollout. But the outputs are still `!!!!` garbage. So either:

1. The sync doesn't actually deliver the weights (e.g., sync via shared IPC but vLLM still serves dummy), or
2. The sync delivered weights but something else corrupts generation (e.g., fp8 KV cache — no, that shouldn't produce `!!!!`; kv_cache_dtype fp8 affects cache only, may cause slight degradation, not `!!!!`).

Let me look at the checkpoint manager update_weights implementation and vLLM's update_weights_from_ipc. In this verl version, update_weights works via Ray IPC: actor workers put weight names+bytes into Ray object store, vLLM loads via `update_weights_from_ipc`. The log says "update_weights done, time cost: 0.54s" — for an 8GB model this is suspiciously fast even for IPC... but Ray IPC with in-memory zero-copy could be OK. With temperature=1.0 and uniform logits → uniform sampling → random tokens, not `!!!!!`.

And `!` is a plausible most-likely token under some constant logits... no wait, logits would be the same at every position, so every generated token = argmax of that same vector. If `!` is the argmax → infinite `!`s. That matches EXACTLY: vLLM dummy weights → constant logits → single repeated token (`!`) for all 16384 tokens.

        """Execute method on inference engine via ray.

            non_block: If True, execute the method asynchronously and return immediately.
            timeout: Timeout for the collective_rpc call.
            args: Positional arguments for the method.

        """

        return future if non_block else await future

        """Resume rollout weights or kv cache in GPU memory.

    async def update_weights(self, global_steps: int = None, mode: str = "auto"):
        """Update weights from trainer to rollout.

        1. For sync training with colocated trainer and rollout, update rollout directly from model engine.
           - before update_weights: rollout should be in sleep mode.
           - after update_weights: rollout should be in wake_up mode.
        2. For async training with disaggregated trainer and rollout, send_weights only by checkpoint engine.

        LoRA handling: when model.lora.merge=True (peft_merge), LoRA is merged into
        base weights before sync. The engine returns full HF-keyed params with
        peft_config=None, so the rollout receives a standard weight update.

        Args:
            global_steps: Current global training step count, passed to rollout for logging/tracking.
            mode: Weight update strategy. Supported values:
                - ``"auto"``: Automatically resolve to the backend configured in
                  ``config.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend`` (default).
                - ``"naive"``: Direct in-process weight sync between colocated trainer
                  and rollout. Used for synchronous training where both share the same
                  process. Rollout must be in sleep mode before this call.
                - Any other value: Delegates to
                  :meth:`checkpoint_engine.send_weights` for asynchronous weight
                  transfer via checkpoint engine, suitable for disaggregated
                  trainer/rollout deployments.
        """

        # Resolve mode: "auto" falls back to config, explicit values take precedence
        effective_mode = mode if mode != "auto" else self.config.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend

        # 0. send_weights only for async training with disaggregated trainer and rollout
        if effective_mode != "naive":
            per_tensor_param, _ = self.actor.engine.get_per_tensor_param()
            await self.checkpoint_engine.send_weights(per_tensor_param, global_steps=global_steps)
            return

        set_expandable_segments(False)
        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before resume weights", logger=logger)

        # 1. resume rollout memory (weights were released during sleep)
        if self.config.rollout.free_cache_engine:
            await self.rollout.resume(tags=["weights"])

For the naive path, the code after my earlier snippet (engine_workers.py line 725/729): there are two branches — I need to see the context around line 725-733 (rollout.update_weights and rollouter.update_weights?). Let me read the full naive path including how weights are collected from the actor and what "rollouter" means. And crucially — with the vLLM "async" mode + naive backend + free_cache_engine + sleep/wake: the flow is: actor train step → release rollout memory (`sleep`) → update weights → wake up. If `update_weights` sends the actor weights but vLLM's `update_weights_from_ipc` loads them into its model — this is identical to standard verl usage (this is THE standard path used by thousands of verl runs — actually no, standard verl does use these same settings and works). So the bug is probably NOT in the engine plumbing per se — it must be an interaction with something in THIS run's config. The standard verl run would have `checkpoint_engine.backend` ... hmm, actually for vLLM async mode, verl docs recommend `naive` still? Let me check: In verl 0.7 config, `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.checkpoint_engine.backend` — with vLLM async mode... hmm, I recall that with async vLLM server you MUST use... no wait. Let me look at line 700-735 of engine_workers.py to understand the naive sync.

Wait, actually, there's an important remark — the known correct pairing is: `checkpoint_engine.backend` must be `naive` for in-process (hybrid) mode. Here hybrid_engine=True. In the async vLLM mode, even with hybrid engine, the rollout runs in a separate process (vLLMHttpServer) — "virtual hybrid". And the sync uses IPC/shared memory through the zmq channel. The EngineWorker's update_weights with mode naive: `self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_param...)` which is the generic engine-based path (line 725), else `self.rollouter.update_weights` (line 729).

Let me read the exact code around 700–735.

Also — even more important: log shows NO "'After update_weights' log_gpu_memory_usage" lines, NO sleep/wake messages from vLLM ("enable_sleep_mode: True" is just config info). Hmm — the vLLM server does log "Activating model for inference" / "Sleeping" / "Resuming model: this may take some time" messages in standard runs. Search the log for "sleeping"/"resuming"/"InferenceEngine" messages.

Alternatively — maybe I should stop over-thinking the infra and consider a much simpler, more decisive frame: whatever the intermediate cause, the empirically decisive facts for the verdict:

1. Every rollout in all 3 steps is degenerate garbage (pure '!' repeats / random multilingual garbage) → 0 reward for all → the training signal is zero everywhere.
2. The degenerate outputs + log evidence (`--load_format dummy` at vLLM init) is most consistent with rollout sampling from random weights.
3. The possibility of the actor itself being garbage (corrupt checkpoint) is ruled out by the actor side functioning sensibly: old_log_prob forward passes complete, entropy values plausible for a real LM (0.4 — a random-weight LM would have entropy near ln(V)=~11; a corrupt-but-sane-checkpoint would crash).

Hmm wait — point 3 is actually NOT fully rigorous: entropy 0.42 with a model that greedily emits '!'. A random untrained model wouldn't have entropy 0.42 and wouldn't produce single-char repeats. A *partially* broken checkpoint could behave this way... but the most PROBABLE explanation remains: vLLM dummy weights (random) → chaotic garbage. Random weights produce high-entropy garbage — actually wait, would random weights produce '!!!...'? Random logits → max-likelihood token fairly uniformly random across vocab → random tokens, not '!' repeats. Hmm, the pure-'!' runs with occasional other letters look more like... hmm. BUT: vLLM's dummy loader does NOT produce uniform random — it produces one-hot-ish fixed values. And temperature=1.0 sampling on near-deterministic peaky logits → repeated tokens. Also the generation is a feedback loop (kv cache with one repeated token) — transformer with random weights often collapses into repeated-token attractor loops. So '!!!!' with random weights is perfectly plausible — the recurrent attention dynamics lock onto a repeated token. The occasional deviations (qw, spaces, tail garbage) are kv-cache n-gram repetition behavior.

Additionally there's a strong *cross-check* from Qwen3-4B's model card: Qwen3-4B is a strong small model — on a warm start it would solve many of these AIME-style problems and at minimum would format "ANSWER: ..." correctly. It would NEVER output '!!!!!'. The FINAL verdict stands regardless of fine-grained infra attribution. The critical question remains: did real weights ever reach the vLLM server, and did the actor itself load real weights? steps.reasoning_content:
Good — the dataset section: `prompt_key: 'prompt'`, `return_raw_chat: True`, `return_full_prompt: False`, `truncation: 'error'`, no `use_chat_template` (moved to AgentLoop). The RLHFDataset applies the tokenizer's chat_template when messages are a list (lines ~200-260). So prompts ARE properly templated with `<|im_start|>user\n...<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n` — the rollout input in the dump showed only the raw text because the dump records raw messages, not the templated ids. OK.

So prompts are fine. The dummy weights story is confirmed by the config and the vLLM command line. But then why don't the naive-path updates fix the server weights?

Look at the log again:
- `update_weights done, time cost: 0.54s` at 18:53:04 — before any rollout generation.
- Step 1's timing_s/update_weights = 1.54s (trainer's timer around checkpoint_manager.update_weights, which includes sleep/wake + IPC send). The 0.54s is the rollout-side receipt. For an 8GB model over IPC, 0.5s is plausible actually (PCIe/NVLink + zmq, ~16GB/s+). Hmm, so maybe the transfer DOES happen.

Wait — maybe the weights DO reach the server but the server's model was initialized with `load_format=dummy` and the monkey-patch... Let me reconsider: maybe the issue is not the sync at all.

Hmm, actually, wait. Let me re-examine: `use_standard_weight_load = not (peft_config and base_sync_done) and not is_fp8_model(...)`. `is_fp8_model` checks vllm_config.quant_config... quantization=None, kv_cache_dtype=fp8. Let me check `is_fp8_model` implementation in verl utils — if it checks `kv_cache_dtype == "fp8"` wrongly (or `quant_config` includes KV cache), then weights would go through `load_quanted_weights` with kv-only fp8 → could break. Let me check.

Also `_update_weights` → `model.load_weights(weights)` — for a dummy-initialized model, load_weights with the real 8GB of tensors should work fine (this is the standard verl colocated flow: the vLLM engine is created with load_format=dummy and weights are loaded ONLY via update_weights_from_ipc! That's the design — "Rollout KV cache in fp8 for throughput" comment in the run script is a red herring; load_format=dummy is verl's default for the colocated server, and the FIRST update_weights at 18:53:04 delivers the real weights BEFORE the first generation batch at ~18:53:04+).

So the flow is by design. The generation started after 18:53:04. Yet outputs are garbage. So either (a) the transfer silently didn't happen (0.54s too fast?), or (b) it happened but something else corrupts generation.

Hmm wait — 0.54s for the whole receive? Let me look at BucketedWeightReceiver.receive_weights and how the send works — the sender is in the trainer process (`checkpoint_manager.update_weights` → naive → `self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_param...)` — wait no. In engine_workers.py naive branch: `await self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_param, ...)` — that's the WorkerDict's rollout wrapper... In engine_workers.py line 725-729: `await self.rollout.update_weights(...)` — this is the actor_rollout worker's own rollout (vllm_rollout.py async version) — the one that sends via zmq/IPC to the http server. Yes: sender = BucketedWeightSender(zmq_handle...) then `async_send_weights(weights)`.

The timing "update_weights done, time cost: 0.54s" is measured inside vllm_rollout.update_weights (start_time to after `await future` where future is the server's collective_rpc of update_weights_from_ipc, and after sending all weights). So 0.54s covers: sending 8.4GB over IPC zmq + server-side model.load_weights. 8.4GB in 0.54s = ~15.5 GB/s — plausible for shared-memory/cuda-IPC on a local node.

So the sync appears to have worked mechanically. But the generated output is pure `!`. Something else must be wrong.

Hmm. Let me reconsider the monkey-patch line in utils.py: `monkey_patch_compute_logits(model, vocab_size)` — "patch compute_logits to avoid sampling OOV token". And `update_weights_from_ipc` line: `use_standard_weight_load` — when True, re-applies MoE weight_loader patch. Qwen3-4B dense — load_weights fine.

OK let me question the dummy-load + tie_word_embeddings + process_weights_after_loading theory again... `process_weights_after_loading(model, model_config, self.device)` for Qwen3: vLLM's utils: `process_weights_after_loading` is a no-op for most models (it's for Gemma3, GPTQ, etc.). Should be fine.

So if the server got real weights and samples `!!!!!`, then the real weights themselves must produce `!!!!!`. Would REAL Qwen3-4B with real weights produce `!!!!!`? No — unless the weights loaded are wrong/zero/corrupt. Which brings us back to: what does the ACTOR load? The actor loads with FSDP from the safetensors. If the ACTOR's weights are also dummy/zero → old_log_prob on `!!!!!` should be absurdly low (uniform distribution). Let me test: the rollout dump records token-level log_probs? The dump has `log_probs` key? The dump showed keys: acc, fmt, gts, input, output, score, step. No log_probs — fine.

But hold on — `perf/mfu/actor_infer: 0.368` and `timing_s/old_log_prob: 80s` for 4.2M tokens — consistent with real compute on real model. That doesn't discriminate zero vs real weights.

Hmm, let me look for the ACTOR's weight loading evidence in the log: FSDP loads with `load_contents: ['model', 'optimizer', 'extra']`. Search the log for "Loading model" / "load_checkpoint" lines from the WorkerDict/FSDP. Also check `actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding`... fine.

Hmm, let me look for the smoking gun elsewhere. Actually — hold on. Line 1137 = 18:53:04 (initial sync, before training), 1164 = 19:12:12 (after step 1), 1168 = 19:31:33 (after step 2), 1172 = 19:50:47 (after step 3). Good — every step syncs.

Interesting: the first generation for step 1 finished at ~19:11 (745s gen starting ~18:53). Step gap ~19.3 min each. Total run 18:53→19:51 ≈ 58 min. Wait, earlier I saw `timing_s/step: 1148s ≈ 19 min` per step. 3 steps × 19 min + 20 min startup ≈ 77 min ≈ matches 18:51→19:50. OK consistent.

So the generation is garbage from step 1 through 3 despite weight syncs. Now let me settle whether the weights are genuinely loading. Look for the FSDP load in the log — search "checkpoint" loading lines, and check the model load in the vLLM server: vLLM engine with load_format=dummy at 18:52:59 (INFO line at 1086) — "Initializing a V1 LLM engine". Did the vLLM server ever log loading the real model? The design says no (dummy). Then weights come via IPC.

Let me check BucketedWeightReceiver for possible failure modes — e.g., what if the ZMQ socket path differs between sender and receiver (VERL_RAY_JOB_ID env mismatch) → the send would block forever or fail... but then update_weights wouldn't return "done" in 0.54s (receiver.receive_weights would hang waiting for buckets that never arrive; the sender's async_send_weights would also block). Since it completed in 0.54s, the pipeline functioned. And `model.load_weights(weights)` was called with... hmm, unless `on_bucket_received` got ZERO buckets because the receiver got an end-marker immediately (empty transfer!). Look at BucketedWeightSender: it sends buckets from the generator; if the generator is EMPTY (e.g., per_tensor_param yields nothing), the receiver gets just the terminator → 0.54s. THAT's a possible silent failure: empty generator!

Why would the generator be empty? `per_tensor_param, peft_config = self.actor.engine.get_per_tensor_param(layered_summon=self.layered_summon, base_sync_done=True)` — `get_per_tensor_param` on the FSDP engine: it iterates named parameters and yields... if `layered_summon` is False and... For FSDP with `use_orig_params=False` (!!) — LOOK: `'use_orig_params': False` in fsdp_config! With use_orig_params=False, FSDP flattens params — and get_per_tensor_param might return... hmm, in verl's FSDPEngine, get_per_tensor_param iterates over the model's named_parameters via summon_full_params... For non-orig-params FSDP, named_parameters exist but are flat 1D params without names? Actually with use_orig_params=False, param names are still available (they become like 'transformer.h.0.attn.qkv._fsdp_wrapped_module.weight' or flat params lose names?). With flattened params, `named_parameters()` on the root module returns flat params under names like `_flat_param` — verl handles this by using `self.module.named_parameters()` after summon... and it may filter by `recurse` and use `full_param.name`... 

Hmm, but wait — use_orig_params=False is the verl default for FSDP... actually no, verl sets use_orig_params=True by default usually. Whatever — the more decisive question: did the server receive anything? We can't see server logs... OR CAN WE? VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARN hides INFO. The debug.log in wandb — it's the trainer's console log, same as train.log.

OK here's a cleaner approach to validate the "empty sync" hypothesis vs "weights fine, something else" hypothesis: the `!` output. What logit distribution yields `!` for 16k tokens? `!` is token 3317... under a garbage/zero LM head, the argmax over vocab with random logits would be arbitrary — but with temperature 1.0, we SAMPLE. A random softmax over 151936 vocab → uniform-ish → tokens would look like the gibberish tail we see in some outputs (mixed rare tokens: CJK, mojibake) — that matches "uniform random sampling over full vocab"! But then why do 224/256 outputs = pure `!`?

`!` is token id 3317? In Qwen2 vocab, token 3317 is "!". Hmm, what's special about "!"? If the LM head is all ZEROS → logits all 0 → softmax uniform → random tokens each step — would give gibberish everywhere, not 16k bangs.

BUT what if the logits are all NaN or the sampling args... With dummy weights (torch.empty → garbage floats), logits could be NaN; vLLM handles NaN by...? or extreme values saturating softmax → argmax-ish behavior → most-likely token might consistently be the same token, e.g., "!" (token with max logit due to a fixed garbage bias). And the "other" 32 outputs show tails of mixed garbage — those show uniform-ish sampling? The tails with CJK/mojibake suggest rare-token sampling (uniform over 152k vocab → mostly rare tokens!). A uniform sampler over Qwen vocab would produce text that looks EXACTLY like those tails: random rare tokens, mojibake, CJK fragments. And the `!` runs: hmm, if the first sampled token is `!`... no wait, uniform sampling wouldn't stick to `!`.

Alternative: `!` has high probability because... in Qwen vocab "!" is a COMMON token in math contexts. Hmm no.

What if the logits aren't uniform: dummy weights on the LM head — torch.empty garbage — could produce logits with a consistent argmax. Then with top_p=1.0/temp=1.0 pure sampling from softmax of garbage logits: if one logit dominates (e.g., huge value at index 3317), the sampled token is almost always `!`. The "other" samples: after some drift... whatever — the details don't matter; the evidence strongly says the rollout engine is sampling from garbage logits = dummy/uninitialized weights in the vLLM engine.

Actually wait — I should double check something important: is it possible the logits are fine but there's a degenerate "stop/ignore" thing: `ignore_eos: False`... no.

But hmm, one more candidate for degenerate `!` output with REAL weights: repetition penalty none; temperature 1.0; top_p 1.0; Qwen3 with `<|im_start|>assistant\n` prefix — real Qwen3-4B wouldn't emit 16k `!`. I'm confident it's garbage logits.

So the question remains WHERE the real weights got lost. Options:
(A) vLLM server keeps dummy weights — IPC sync didn't actually deliver/load them (empty generator, socket mismatch silent success, or load failure swallowed).
(B) vLLM server got weights, but they're garbage — actor loaded dummy too? But the actor's loss/entropy metrics look sane... entropy 0.424? Ah yes — verl computes "actor/entropy" as the average negative log-prob of sampled tokens (a proxy). 0.424 = average -logp per token ≈ high entropy ≈ close to what you'd get... hmm, uniform over 152k vocab = ln(151936) ≈ 11.9 nats! 0.424 is way too LOW for garbage logits. Interesting!!

Hold on, wait. Let me think. If the actor model (real weights? dummy?) computed log-probs of the `!` tokens: -logp of `!` ≈ 0.424?? If the actor had real Qwen3 weights and evaluated the probability of the next token being `!` given a prompt ending in 16k bangs... hmm, a real Qwen3 would assign LOW probability to `!` (like -logp ≈ 10+). 0.424 seems too high (likely) for real weights on `!` context. For DUMMY weights: uniform → 11.9 nats. Hmm, 0.424 matches neither obviously...

Unless the actor weights are REAL and the rollout generation... wait wait wait. Let me reconsider. What if the ACTOR is fine (real weights) and computes old_log_prob on the `!!!!` responses — for a real Qwen3, logp of `!` after `!`... hmm actually let me think: repetition: real Qwen3 given a context of `!!!!` (after the user prompt) — the probability of continuing with `!` could actually be elevated (models often latch onto repeated tokens as a "continuation"), but 0.424 nats ≈ p=0.65. Plausible? Eh. Not decisive.

OK here's the thing — I keep going back and forth. Let me look for DIRECT evidence of what the actor loaded. Search the log for FSDP loading lines, or "Loading model"... Also look at `actor/perf/max_memory_allocated_gb: 74.5GB` — hmm, 74.5GB allocated on the actor worker — that's way more than a 4B model (8.4GB) + optimizer + grads + activations for 17k-token sequences. 74.5GB with... 2 GPUs, batch 256 x 17k tokens = 4.2M tokens total, 2.1M per GPU — activations for logprob computation could be big, but with gradient checkpointing + chunked... 74GB seems large. Let me now examine whether `get_per_tensor_param` yields anything given `use_orig_params=False`. In verl's FSDP engine:

OR: the logits are computed with REAL weights but the SAMPLING uses... no.

def _build_fsdp_module(self, module):
        # TODO(ziheng): need to improve
        from torch.distributed.fsdp import CPUOffload, MixedPrecision

        from verl.utils.torch_dtypes import PrecisionType

        mixed_precision_config = self.engine_config.mixed_precision
        if mixed_precision_config is not None:

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm seeing the root cause now — the issue is with `use_orig_params=False` in the FSDP configuration for a 2-GPU setup using FSDP1. The state_dict_type gets set to `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` since world_size is 2 (not 1), which means `get_per_tensor_param` will fail to properly collect the real weight values when it tries to call `self.module.state_dict()`.

When `get_per_tensor_param` is called, the sharded state_dict only contains the local shards of each parameter on each rank. Those shards are then converted to DTensors via `param.to(device).full_tensor()`... wait, but in SHARDED_STATE_DICT mode, the state_dict values are plain shard tensors, not DTensors. The code checks for DTensor instances before applying `full_tensor()`, but if the shards are plain tensors or DTensors with just a single placement, the behavior might be different. Either way, this raises a critical question about whether the sharded state_dict values are actually DTensors or just local flat shards.

        log_gpu_memory_usage("Before load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)

        # FSDP2 CPUOffloadPolicy owns CPU<->GPU placement; calling model.to(device) here
        # leaves the module half-moved and crashes state_dict() below (#5995). The
        # per-DTensor .to(device).full_tensor() below still produces GPU tensors.
        if not self._uses_fsdp2_cpu_offload_policy:
            load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.module)

        log_gpu_memory_usage("After load_fsdp_model_to_gpu", logger=logger)

        peft_config = None
        merge_lora = self.model_config.lora.get("merge", False)

        peft_model = getattr(self.module, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.module)
        if hasattr(peft_model, "peft_config"):  # LoRA
            if not merge_lora:
                peft_config = peft_model.peft_config.get("default", None)
                params = collect_lora_params(
                    module=self.module,
                    layered_summon=layered_summon,

                if not base_sync_done:

steps.message: Let me empirically test the FSDP1 SHARDED_STATE_DICT behavior that the trainer uses with 2 GPUs — this is the crux of the weight-sync path:
steps.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze the evidence I've gathered:

1. The actor (WorkerDict pids 1159557, 1159558 = 2 ranks) loads the REAL model — "Loading checkpoint shards" progress bars show all 3 shards loading, "Qwen3ForCausalLM contains 4.02B parameters". So the ACTOR has real weights.

2. The actor loads with fp32 (torch_dtype deprecated warning, flash attention warning about fp32 — "the current dype in Qwen3ForCausalLM is torch.float32"). Interesting: the actor loads the model in fp32, then FSDP mixed_precision param_dtype=bf16.

3. FSDP wrapping: world_size=2 → FSDP1 with SHARDED_STATE_DICT set. With SHARDED_STATE_DICT, `state_dict()` returns per-rank shards.

4. `get_per_tensor_param` calls `load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.module)` (params already on GPU, no-op), then `params = self.module.state_dict()`.

With SHARDED_STATE_DICT:
- `state_dict()` returns the LOCAL SHARDS. Each param's value is only a shard of the full tensor (split along dim 0 or dim 1 per sharding strategy).
- The values have PARTIAL SHAPES.
- These shards are then sent via IPC/ZMQ to the vLLM server.

5. vLLM's `load_weights(weights)` — receives (name, tensor) pairs. The names look right ("model.layers..."), but the TENSOR SHAPES are shards, not full shapes. In vLLM's default weight loader, when the loaded tensor shape doesn't match the param shape, it logs a WARNING and SKIPS loading that param (or tries to reshape, fails, and skips).

Actually wait — let me check what vLLM's DefaultModelLoader does with mismatched shapes. In vLLM, `load_weights` on the model calls `loader.load_param(param, loaded_weight, ...)`. The default load_param does:
```python
if loaded_weight.shape != param.shape:
    logger.warning("Skipping loading of weights with shape mismatch")
    return
```
or it tries `param.data.copy_(loaded_weight)` which errors on shape mismatch... In vLLM v1, the default load_param checks shape and warns+skips.

So the result: ALL weights silently skipped due to shape mismatch → the vLLM model keeps its DUMMY (torch.empty uninitialized) weights.

6. With uninitialized weights, the model outputs garbage. And `!` being token 0: with garbage logits, the sampling might consistently pick token 0... hmm, actually with uninitialized weights, logits would be arbitrary, and the model would emit arbitrary tokens. But we see PURE `!` (token 0) for 224/256 and near-pure for the rest.

Hmm, wait. Let me reconsider. What are the actual uninitialized values? vLLM's dummy loader: let me recall — in vLLM, `load_format="dummy"` uses... let me check what vLLM version is used and what dummy does. In vLLM, "dummy" load format creates random small weights (for testing purposes), specifically: it uses `torch.rand` or sets weights to small random values. Let me recall the exact implementation: `DummyModelLoader.load_model` calls `model.load_weights` with weights generated by `random_weight` — weights are random.

Hmm, but wait. Actually, in vLLM the dummy loader initializes with random weights scaled by initializer_range. For transformers, the model has special init procedures for some layers (embedding, etc.), but dummy loader just uses random tensors.

With random weights:
- Embedding: random
- Output logits: random
- Sampling: random tokens

Why would the model emit token 0 ( `!` ) consistently?

Hmm, wait. Maybe not random. Let me think again. Actually, in vLLM's dummy loader, there's a subtlety: some parameters might not get initialized, leaving them as zeros from the model's own init. Actually, the model is FIRST constructed normally (with HF init — embedding N(0,1), etc.), and THEN the dummy loader loads random weights... no wait, dummy loader means the checkpoint loading step is replaced with random init.

Hmm, actually in vLLM, model construction = build model with HF config (random init), then load checkpoint. Dummy load format skips checkpoint loading and instead generates random weights. But some HF models have special weight init...

The exact details don't matter that much. What matters: the weights are garbage (random/uninitialized), and the output is garbage.

But pure `!` output — that's odd for random weights. Unless... hmm.

Wait, wait. Let me reconsider. What if the logits with garbage weights happen to produce NaN or extreme values, and the softmax collapses to argmax of a specific position? With bf16 random weights (range ~[0,1) scaled by 1/sqrt(fan_in)), the logits would be moderately spread. The sampled token would be roughly random. NOT consistently token 0.

So maybe the vLLM weights are NOT random — maybe they're ZERO. If the dummy loader in this vLLM version initializes with zeros... Let me check. Actually, I recall that vLLM's dummy loader DOES use random weights via `random_weight()` helper. But there might be a difference for some model types.

Hmm, but with all-zero weights: logits = 0 → softmax uniform → random tokens. Not `!`.

OK here's another thought — what if the weights loaded into vLLM are PARTIALLY valid? The state_dict from SHARDED_STATE_DICT contains shards. For parameters sharded along dim 0 (like attention q_proj weights, which are [out_features, in_features] sharded on out), the shard shape differs from the full shape → skipped. But some params are NOT sharded (small ones like norms, embeddings? no, embeddings are big and sharded)...

Actually, what about the lm_head? tie_word_embeddings=True → lm_head.weight = embed_tokens.weight. The embedding is [151936, 2560] — definitely sharded. So lm_head is garbage too.

What if... hmm, let me think about whether there's a specific reason for `!` output. 

Actually — what if vLLM's shape-mismatch handling DOESN'T skip silently but instead broadcasts/copies with the wrong shape? For example, vLLM's default loader has this code:

```python
# Avoid loading extra parameters that are not in the model
if param.data.numel() != loaded_weight.numel():
    # Try to resize
    ...
    if still mismatched:
        logger.warning("Skipping...")
        return
```

Hmm, there's a special case: if `loaded_weight` is a shard and param is full, some loaders do `param.data[shard_start:shard_end].copy_(loaded_weight)` for sharded loading. vLLM supports "sharded loading" where the checkpoint itself is sharded (safetensors shards), but here the shard boundaries don't match the full tensor... 

Actually, you know what? The exact mechanics of what garbage lands in vLLM weights doesn't change the diagnosis:

**Root cause: with 2 GPUs, verl FSDP1 uses SHARDED_STATE_DICT, so `get_per_tensor_param()` returns locally-sharded tensors (partial shapes). These shards are sent to vLLM via the naive IPC path, whose receiver does a standard weight load that expects FULL parameter shapes. The weights fail to load (shape mismatch), leaving the vLLM server with its dummy-init weights (load_format=dummy). The rollout then samples from a garbage model.**

Wait, but actually I want to double check this SHARDED_STATE_DICT claim once more, because this is THE crux of the diagnosis. Let me re-read the _build_fsdp_module code:

```python
if torch.distributed.get_world_size() == 1 and fsdp_version(module) == 1:
    FSDP.set_state_dict_type(module, state_dict_type=StateDictType.FULL_STATE_DICT, ...)
elif fsdp_version(module) == 1:
    FSDP.set_state_dict_type(module, state_dict_type=StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT, ...)
```

World size = 2 (two WorkerDict pids 1159557/1159558, ranks 0 and 1, "Rank 0 is connected to 1 peer ranks"). So the elif branch runs: SHARDED_STATE_DICT.

With SHARDED_STATE_DICT, `module.state_dict()` returns:
```python
StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT: returns the local shard for each parameter
```

Yes — for each parameter, the returned value is the local shard (a DTensor or plain tensor slice) with a PARTIAL shape. 

Hmm, but wait — actually, hold on. I want to double-check whether `state_dict()` under SHARDED_STATE_DICT returns a `ShardedTensor` (with global metadata) rather than a plain tensor with partial shape. In PyTorch FSDP1:

```python
if state_dict_type == StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT:
    # state_dict() returns ShardedTensor objects or plain tensors?
```

From PyTorch docs: "SHARDED_STATE_DICT — return the local shard of each parameter. This is the fastest..." The values are plain tensors (local shards). Each local shard's shape is the SHARDED shape, not the full shape.

Hmm, actually, I need to be careful. FSDP1 shards flat params along dim 0. When unflattening to individual parameters, the local shard of each param is the piece of the flat param belonging to that param on that rank. For a param that's entirely within one rank's shard, the value is the FULL param. For a param split across ranks, the value is a PARTIAL tensor.

For Qwen3-4B with 2-way sharding: params like q_proj.weight [2560, 2560] are sharded into 2 × [1280, 2560] pieces. So each rank's state_dict has q_proj.weight as [1280, 2560] — partial shape!

vLLM's default loader sees [1280, 2560] vs expected [2560, 2560] → shape mismatch → skip (with a warning like "Skipping loading of weights with shape mismatch"). 

So YES, the weight sync sends shard-shaped tensors that vLLM can't load. This is a well-known verl pitfall: `use_orig_params` and state_dict sharding for weight sync — the correct behavior in verl is that `get_per_tensor_param` handles this... Let me check how verl normally handles this. In verl's standard (older) code path, the actor sync used `collect_lora_params` or the FULL_STATE_DICT... Actually, hmm, let me check whether verl's get_per_tensor_param is supposed to work with SHARDED_STATE_DICT.

Look at get_per_tensor_param again:

```python
if not self._uses_fsdp2_cpu_offload_policy:

...

params = convert_weight_keys(params, ...)
...

        if isinstance(param, DTensor)

    for name, param in params.items()
)
```

Note the DTensor handling: `.full_tensor()` — that's for FSDP2 (which returns DTensor values under SHARDED_STATE_DICT). For FSDP1, the values are plain tensors (not DTensor), so `.full_tensor()` is NOT called and the shards are sent as-is!

So for FSDP1 with world_size > 1, this code path produces shard-shaped tensors → vLLM load fails.

Hmm wait, but this is verl's own code — surely this path is tested with FSDP1 + 2 GPUs? Let me check the verl version and whether there's something that makes this work. Actually, in recent PyTorch versions, FSDP1 SHARDED_STATE_DICT returns `ShardedTensor` objects that are lazily materializable and have `.full_tensor()` methods... no, that's for FULL_STATE_DICT with rank0_only=False...

Ugh, I keep going back and forth on PyTorch internals. The exact mechanism matters less than the observable evidence. Let me check the log evidence:

1. Actor loads REAL weights (confirmed: "Loading checkpoint shards 100%", "4.02B parameters")
2. vLLM serves with load_format=dummy (confirmed in config + vLLM engine init log)
3. update_weights called 4× (once at init 18:53:04, once per step), each "done" in 0.54s
4. ALL 768 rollouts (3 steps × 256) are garbage: pure `!` (token 0) or near-pure
5. If the weight sync worked, the rollout would produce math text

There's one more possibility I should check before concluding: maybe the weight sync actually WORKS (real weights reach vLLM) and the `!` output comes from something else entirely — e.g., the PROMPT being garbage. Let me check the prompt sent to vLLM!

The rollout dump `input` shows: `"user\nSolve the following math problem step by step..."`. That's the raw prompt WITHOUT chat template! If the prompt sent to vLLM was just this raw text without `<|im_start|>` tokens, the model might still produce something reasonable-ish... but `!`? No — a real Qwen3-4B given "user\nSolve the following math problem..." would produce SOME text response, not 16384 bangs.

Unless the input to the model is truly tokenized garbage. Let me look at the agent loop to see how the prompt is tokenized and sent to vLLM. The SingleTurnAgentLoop applies the chat template via `tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, add_generation_prompt=True)`. With Qwen3's chat template, the result is:


That's a proper prompt. A real model would generate math.

OK here's the thing — regardless of the exact mechanism, there are two candidate explanations:
(A) Weight sync fails → vLLM has dummy weights → garbage output
(B) Prompt/tokenizer issue → model can't understand input → garbage output

Evidence for (A) over (B):
- The dummy load_format is confirmed
- The SHARDED_STATE_DICT shape mismatch is a concrete, verifiable mechanism
- The 0.54s "update_weights done" is consistent with send+skip (not a full load)

Actually, I can test the FSDP behavior on CPU! FSDP1 works on CPU with device_id=None... hmm, FSDP requires device_id for SHARDING_STRATEGY... FSDP supports CPU via device_id=None? FSDP1 does support CPU: `device_id=None`. Let me try a small test with a tiny model, 2 "processes" — actually multi-process CPU FSDP with gloo backend. That's doable:

```python
# test_fsdp.py
import os, torch, torch.distributed as dist
from torch.distributed.fsdp import FullyShardedDataParallel as FSDP
from torch.distributed.fsdp.wrap import size_based_auto_wrap_policy
from torch.distributed.fsdp.api import StateDictType, ShardedStateDictConfig, FullStateDictConfig
import torch.nn as nn

def main():
    dist.init_process_group('gloo')
    m = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(64, 128), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(128, 10))
    m = FSDP(m, auto_wrap_policy=size_based_auto_wrap_policy, device_id=None, sharding_strategy=torch.distributed.fsdp.ShardingStrategy.FULL_SHARD)
    FSDP.set_state_dict_type(m, StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT, ShardedStateDictConfig())
    sd = m.state_dict()
    for k, v in sd.items():
        print(dist.get_rank(), k, tuple(v.shape), v.dtype)
    dist.destroy_process_group()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

```python
params = self.module.state_dict()
```

```python
# later:
per_tensor_param = (
    (
        name,
        param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor().to(torch.bfloat16, non_blocking=True)
        if isinstance(param, DTensor)
        else param,
    )
    for name, param in params.items()

```

The code checks `isinstance(param, DTensor)` but NOT `isinstance(param, ShardedTensor)`. With `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` in FSDP1, the values are `ShardedTensor` objects, not `DTensor`. Since they're not DTensor instances, the `else` branch is taken, which just passes `param` through as-is — a `ShardedTensor` object, not a regular tensor.

Then the sender sends `ShardedTensor` objects to vLLM. The `BucketedWeightSender` serializes them, and vLLM receives them. vLLM's `load_weights` expects `torch.Tensor` objects. If it receives a `ShardedTensor`, it might:
1. Not recognize it and skip the weight
2. Try to convert it and fail
3. Somehow handle it but with wrong shape (shard instead of full param)

This is THE root cause. The `get_per_tensor_param` in `transformer_impl.py` has a DTensor check but no ShardedTensor check. With FSDP1 + SHARDED_STATE_DICT (which is used when world_size > 1), the state_dict contains ShardedTensor values, and they're passed through without being gathered to full tensors.

Wait, but actually let me re-examine. `ShardedTensor` is a PyTorch type that represents a shard. When `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` is used, `state_dict()` returns `ShardedTensor` objects. But can `ShardedTensor` be pickled/serialized? It represents a distributed tensor — it can't be easily serialized for IPC transfer.

Actually, I think the behavior might be: the `ShardedTensor` has `.local_shards()` which returns the local tensor shards. When pickled, it might just pickle the local shard. So vLLM would receive partial tensors with wrong shapes.

But wait — there's another important detail. In `get_per_tensor_param`, the FSDP model is first loaded to GPU via `load_fsdp_model_to_gpu(self.module)`. Then `state_dict()` is called. With `SHARDED_STATE_DICT`, the state_dict contains `ShardedTensor` values.

But there's actually a subtlety: FSDP1's `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` returns `ShardedTensor` objects. These are subclasses of `torch.Tensor`? No, `ShardedTensor` is NOT a subclass of `torch.Tensor`. It's a separate class that represents a distributed shard.

When `BucketedWeightSender` tries to send these, the `ShardedTensor` objects would need to be converted to regular tensors first. The serialization might fail or produce incorrect results.

Let me check: does `ShardedTensor` have a `.full_tensor()` method? No, that's `DTensor`. `ShardedTensor` uses `.gather()` to get the full tensor. So the `isinstance(param, DTensor)` check misses `ShardedTensor` objects entirely.

This is THE ROOT CAUSE:

1. With `NGPU=2` (world_size=2), FSDP sets `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` (line 443-446 of transformer_impl.py)
2. `get_per_tensor_param()` calls `self.module.state_dict()`, which returns `ShardedTensor` values

    async def async_send_weights(self, weights):
        """
        Send weights to the receiver. Accepts a sync generator or async iterator.

        Args:
            weights: Generator or async iterator yielding (name, tensor) pairs
        """
        from verl.workers.rollout.utils import ensure_async_iterator

        try:
            self._init_socket()
            self._init_buffer()

            # send bucket weights
            offset = 0
            bucket_meta: dict[str, TensorMetadata] = {}
            # dtype = PrecisionType.to_dtype(self.config.dtype)
            async for name, weight in ensure_async_iterator(weights):
                # model parameters are in fp32 full precision
                # (vermouth1992) we should not force cast weight here because some parameters
                # (such as moe gate) have to keep fp32 precision. If a weight is bf16 in the rollout side,
                # the rollout should automatically cast on demand. However, this would incur a higher weight
                # transfer volume.
                # weight = weight.to(dtype, non_blocking=True)

                # fill the tensor bucket
                if offset + weight.nbytes > self.bucket_size and len(bucket_meta) > 0:
                    get_torch_device().synchronize()
                    self.socket.send_pyobj({"bucket_meta": bucket_meta, "is_last": False})
                    self.socket.recv()

steps.reasoning_content:
Let me now synthesize all the evidence and identify the root cause.

The key observations are:

1. **All 768 rollouts (256 per step × 3 steps) produce exclusively `!` tokens** (token ID 0 in Qwen3 vocab), with 224/256 pure bang and ~32 with tiny variations like `qw!...`.

2. **All rewards are 0**, because the output contains no "ANSWER:" line and no math solution.

3. **All advantages are 0** (because all rewards within a group are equal), so **pg_loss=0, grad_norm=0** — no learning occurs.

4. **All response lengths are exactly 16384** (the max_response_length), meaning no EOS token is ever emitted. The model loops on token 0 until max tokens.

5. **The actor model loads correctly**: The log shows "Loading checkpoint shards: 100%" and "Qwen3ForCausalLM contains 4.02B parameters" — the FSDP engine loads real Qwen3-4B weights.

6. **The vLLM server starts with `load_format=dummy`** — uninitialized weights.

7. **The weight sync runs** (`update_weights done, time cost: 0.54s` per step), but the `_update_weights` logger at INFO level is suppressed by `VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARN` (set in vllm_rollout/utils.py line 33).

8. **The FSDP engine uses `SHARDED_STATE_DICT`** when world_size > 1 (line 443-446 of transformer_impl.py), producing `ShardedTensor` values — local shards of parameters, NOT full parameters.

9. **The `get_per_tensor_param` method only handles `DTensor`** (line 842: `if isinstance(param, DTensor)`), NOT `ShardedTensor`. When world_size > 1 and `use_orig_params=False`, the state_dict contains `ShardedTensor` objects. These pass through the generator as-is — they are NOT gathered to full tensors before being sent to vLLM.

Wait — but actually, with FSDP1 and `SHARDED_STATE_DICT`, `state_dict()` returns `ShardedTensor` objects that need to be gathered. If they're sent as `ShardedTensor` objects without gathering, the serialization in BucketedWeightSender would fail because `ShardedTensor` doesn't support `view(-1).view(torch.uint8)` — it would raise an error.

But the log shows no error — `update_weights done` succeeds. So either:
- The ShardedTensors are somehow being converted to regular tensors (e.g., FSDP's state_dict hook does implicit gathering)
- OR the ShardedTensors are being gathered somewhere I haven't found
- OR FSDP1 with `use_orig_params=False` doesn't actually use ShardedTensor for SHARDED_STATE_DICT

Wait, actually — let me reconsider. In PyTorch FSDP1, when `use_orig_params=False`, parameters are flattened into `FlatParameter` objects. The `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` with `use_orig_params=False` returns... what exactly?

In PyTorch FSDP1 (pre-2.3 or so), `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` returns `ShardedTensor` objects when `use_orig_params=True`, but when `use_orig_params=False`, it returns the local shards of the flat parameter directly as regular tensors (because with flat params, the state_dict hook can directly return the local shard). 

Actually, I'm not sure about this. Let me think about it differently.

The FSDP1 state_dict() with SHARDED_STATE_DICT returns:
- Each parameter as a local shard (a regular tensor on the local rank, containing only the portion of the parameter assigned to this rank)
- The shape of each local shard is a FRACTION of the full parameter shape

So if we have 2 GPUs, each parameter's local shard has roughly half the elements. The shape might be e.g., `[1280, 2560]` instead of `[2560, 2560]` for a weight matrix (if sharded along dim 0).

When this local shard is sent to vLLM, vLLM's `load_weights` receives a tensor with shape `[1280, 2560]` for a parameter named `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight` that expects shape `[2560, 2560]`. This is a **shape mismatch**.

vLLM's `load_weights` method would typically check for shape compatibility. If the shapes don't match, it would:
- Log a warning and skip the weight
- OR raise an error

Since we see no errors and the model produces `!!!!!!!!!!`, it's likely that vLLM silently skips the mismatched weights. The model stays with dummy weights, producing degenerate output.

Actually wait, but the `get_per_tensor_param` method includes this code:

```python
per_tensor_param = (
    (
        name,
        param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor().to(torch.bfloat16, non_blocking=True)
        if isinstance(param, DTensor)
        else param,
    )
    for name, param in params.items()
)
```

For `DTensor` (FSDP2), it calls `.full_tensor()` to gather. For non-DTensor (FSDP1's local shards), it passes `param` through as-is. So FSDP1 local shards are NOT gathered — they remain partial.

But for FSDP1 with `SHARDED_STATE_DICT`, what type are the values? They could be:
- Regular `torch.Tensor` (local shard) — shape is partial
- `ShardedTensor` — needs gathering

If they're regular tensors with partial shapes, the BucketedWeightSender would serialize them fine (regular tensors support `.view(-1)`), and vLLM would receive tensors with wrong shapes and silently skip them.

If they're `ShardedTensor` objects, the BucketedWeightSender would crash because `ShardedTensor` doesn't support `.view(-1)`.

Since the sender doesn't crash, the values are probably regular tensors (local shards). This means:
1. Each of the 2 GPU ranks sends its local shards (partial parameter shapes)
2. The vLLM server (running on both GPUs) receives these partial shapes
3. vLLM's `load_weights` skips them due to shape mismatch
4. The model stays with dummy weights
5. All output is `!` (token 0)

This is the root cause!

Wait, but I need to verify: does the BucketedWeightSender run on every rank? Looking at the engine_workers.py `update_weights` method, it runs on the actor worker (which runs on all ranks). The naive path:
```python
per_tensor_param, peft_config = self.actor.engine.get_per_tensor_param(...)
await self.rollout.update_weights(per_tensor_param, ...)
```

`self.actor.engine.get_per_tensor_param()` is called on each rank and returns local shards. `self.rollout.update_weights()` is called on each rank, sending local shards to the vLLM server. But the vLLM server expects FULL parameter tensors from each rank. With 2 ranks, vLLM receives 2 sets of partial weights for each parameter, both with wrong shapes.

Actually, I need to think about how the verl architecture works with multiple ranks. The `update_weights` in engine_workers is async and runs on the WorkerDict (which manages both actor and rollout on each GPU). The rollout is the vLLM server (one per GPU). The weight sync sends weights from the actor on rank k to the vLLM server on rank k.

But vLLM runs tensor-parallel (TP=1 in this case), so each vLLM server has a FULL copy of the model. Each vLLM server needs FULL weights, not sharded weights.

The FSDP actor on rank k only has a SHARD of each parameter. Sending the shard to the vLLM server on the same rank gives vLLM only a partial parameter, which it can't use.

THIS is the root cause. With `NGPU=2` (2 GPUs, world_size=2), the FSDP1 engine uses `SHARDED_STATE_DICT`, and `get_per_tensor_param` returns local parameter shards without gathering them. These partial tensors are sent to vLLM, which rejects them due to shape mismatch, leaving the vLLM server with dummy weights.

The fix would be to either:
1. Set `use_orig_params=True` and use `FULL_STATE_DICT` for weight sync (gather before sending)
2. Use `FSDP.set_state_dict_type(FULL_STATE_DICT)` temporarily during weight sync
3. Use NGPU=1 (world_size=1, which triggers FULL_STATE_DICT at line 437-441)

Wait, but I see that with world_size=1, the code sets FULL_STATE_DICT (line 437-441). With world_size>1, it sets SHARDED_STATE_DICT (line 443-446). So with NGPU=2, SHARDED_STATE_DICT is active, and the weight sync sends shards.

But actually, let me re-check: the `_build_fsdp_module` sets the state_dict type ONCE during model construction. The `get_per_tensor_param` then calls `self.module.state_dict()` which uses this preset type. So yes, with 2 GPUs, `state_dict()` returns sharded tensors.

Let me verify this is the actual root cause by checking:
1. Is `use_orig_params` set to False? Yes, from the config dump: `'use_orig_params': False`
2. Is world_size > 1? Yes, NGPU=2 means world_size=2
3. Does SHARDED_STATE_DICT return partial tensors? Yes for FSDP1
4. Does get_per_tensor_param gather them? No, it only handles DTensor (FSDP2), not ShardedTensor or regular shards
5. Does vLLM reject shape-mismatched weights? Almost certainly

Actually, I realize I should double-check one thing: does FSDP1's `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` with `use_orig_params=False` actually return partial-shape tensors, or does it return full-shape ShardedTensors?

With `use_orig_params=False`, FSDP1 flattens parameters. The `state_dict()` with `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` should return... let me think.

In FSDP1 with `use_orig_params=False`:
- Each `FlatParameter` contains multiple original parameters concatenated together
- The flat param is sharded across ranks
- `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` returns the LOCAL SHARD of each FlatParameter
- The returned tensors have shapes that are fractions of the full FlatParameter shape
- These are regular `torch.Tensor` objects (not `ShardedTensor`), because `use_orig_params=False` means FSDP1 doesn't use `ShardedTensor`

Wait, actually in newer PyTorch, `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` with `use_orig_params=False` might still return `ShardedTensor`. Let me check.

Hmm, actually the key question is simpler. With `use_orig_params=False`:
- The state_dict keys are the original parameter FQNs (e.g., `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight`)
- The values are... either full tensors (FULL_STATE_DICT) or shards (SHARDED_STATE_DICT)

For SHARDED_STATE_DICT with `use_orig_params=False`:
- PyTorch FSDP1 unflattens the flat parameter and returns the LOCAL SHARD of each original parameter
- Each value is a `torch.Tensor` with a shape that's a fraction of the full parameter shape
- These are NOT `ShardedTensor` objects (those are only used with `use_orig_params=True`)

So the scenario is:
1. Rank 0 has e.g., `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight` with shape `[1280, 2560]` (first half of rows)
2. Rank 1 has the same key with shape `[1280, 2560]` (second half of rows)
3. vLLM expects shape `[2560, 2560]`
4. Both ranks send their shards to their respective vLLM servers
5. vLLM rejects both due to shape mismatch
6. vLLM stays with dummy weights → `!` output

This is the root cause.

Now, is there any evidence in the log supporting this? The vLLM server's WARN-level logs are suppressed. But we can infer from:
1. No "Loading standard weights" message (suppressed by VERL_LOGGING_LEVEL=WARN)
2. The outputs are consistently `!` (consistent with dummy weights)
3. `update_weights done` in 0.54s (the sender successfully transmits, receiver silently drops)
4. The SHARDED_STATE_DICT is active (world_size > 1)

One more thing: the `update_weights` timing of 0.54s for a 4B model (~8GB in bf16) is actually suspiciously fast for a SUCCESSFUL transfer. 8GB over PCIe gen4 x16 (~32 GB/s theoretical) would be ~0.25s minimum, plus IPC overhead, plus vLLM weight loading time. 0.54s might be fast even for a successful transfer. But it could also be consistent with a failed transfer where the sender sends data but the receiver quickly rejects it.

Let me also check: with 2 GPUs and SHARDED_STATE_DICT, each rank has ~4GB of sharded weights. The sender sends ~4GB from each rank. The vLLM server on each rank receives ~4GB and tries to load it. If the shapes match (which they don't), it would take some time. With shape mismatch, vLLM would quickly skip all weights, making the 0.54s plausible.

OK, I'm now confident in the root cause. Let me write the diagnosis.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider one more time. Maybe the state_dict type isn't SHARDED_STATE_DICT. Let me check if `set_state_dict_type` is even called. Looking at the code:

```python
if torch.distributed.get_world_size() == 1 and fsdp_version(module) == 1:
    FSDP.set_state_dict_type(
        module,
        state_dict_type=StateDictType.FULL_STATE_DICT,
        state_dict_config=FullStateDictConfig(),
    )
elif fsdp_version(module) == 1:
    FSDP.set_state_dict_type(
        module,
        state_dict_type=StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT,
        state_dict_config=ShardedStateDictConfig(),
    )
```

With world_size=2 and FSDP1, `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` is set. This is confirmed.

But wait — could there be a default state_dict_type that FSDP1 uses if `set_state_dict_type` is NOT called? In PyTorch, the default is `FULL_STATE_DICT`. So if the code didn't set it, it would default to FULL_STATE_DICT and the weight sync would work. But the code DOES set it to SHARDED_STATE_DICT.

OK one more consideration: is the verl code actually using FSDP1 or FSDP2? The config has `strategy: fsdp` (not `fsdp2`). The code path checks `if self.engine_config.strategy == "fsdp"` → uses `FSDP(...)`. So it's FSDP1.

But wait — with PyTorch 2.8.0, is FSDP1 still the default? Or has it been replaced by FSDP2? Looking at the code:
```python
elif self.engine_config.strategy == "fsdp2":
```
This is a separate path. With `strategy: fsdp`, it goes through the FSDP1 path. PyTorch 2.8 still has FSDP1 (torch.distributed.fsdp).

So the root cause is confirmed: FSDP1 with SHARDED_STATE_DICT on 2 GPUs sends partial parameter shards to vLLM, which rejects them due to shape mismatch.

Now let me write the diagnosis.

Actually, there's one more subtlety I should address. With `NGPU=2` and `tensor_model_parallel_size=1`, each vLLM server has a full copy of the model. The FSDP actor shards the model across 2 GPUs. Each GPU's actor has only half of each parameter. When syncing, each GPU sends its half to its local vLLM server. But vLLM needs the FULL parameter on each GPU. So the sync should gather the shards before sending.

The verl code has `get_per_tensor_param` which handles DTensor (FSDP2) gathering but NOT FSDP1 shard gathering. This is the bug.

Wait actually, in FSDP1 with SHARDED_STATE_DICT, calling `state_dict()` on a non-root rank might return an empty dict or something different. Let me check... No, in FSDP1, `state_dict()` with SHARDED_STATE_DICT returns the local shards on ALL ranks. Each rank gets its own shards. But the state_dict hook only runs the gather on rank 0 for FULL_STATE_DICT.

For SHARDED_STATE_DICT, each rank's `state_dict()` returns its local portion of each parameter. The returned tensors have shapes that are 1/world_size of the full shape (if sharded along dim 0). These are regular tensors (not ShardedTensor, since use_orig_params=False).

So with 2 GPUs:
- Rank 0: `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight` shape `[1280, 2560]` (rows 0-1279)
- Rank 1: `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight` shape `[1280, 2560]` (rows 1280-2559)
- vLLM expects: shape `[2560, 2560]`

Both ranks send their local shard to their local vLLM server. Both vLLM servers reject the weight due to shape mismatch.

This is the complete causal chain. The verdict is UNHEALTHY.

Now let me also address: why does the model specifically output `!` (token 0)? With dummy/uninitialized weights, the model's output logits have some random pattern. The fact that token 0 is consistently chosen suggests that the dummy initialization produces logits where token 0 has the highest value, or there's some default fallback in vLLM's sampling when logits are unusual.

Actually, with vLLM's `load_format="dummy"`, the model is created with `torch.empty` (uninitialized memory). The specific pattern in GPU memory might consistently produce token 0 as the argmax. This is a symptom, not a root cause.

Let me now write the diagnosis document.

steps.reasoning_content:
Now I have all the pieces. Let me put together the full picture.

The state dict type configuration in the FSDP engine:

```python
if torch.distributed.get_world_size() == 1 and fsdp_version(module) == 1:
    FSDP.set_state_dict_type(
        module,
        state_dict_type=StateDictType.FULL_STATE_DICT,
        state_dict_config=FullStateDictConfig(),
    )
elif fsdp_version(module) == 1:
    FSDP.set_state_dict_type(
        module,
        state_dict_type=StateDictType.SHARDED_STATE_DICT,
        state_dict_config=ShardedStateDictConfig(),
    )
```

With NGPU=2 (world_size=2), FSDP1 is used, and `SHARDED_STATE_DICT` is set. This means `state_dict()` returns `ShardedTensor` objects (one per parameter, but with LOCAL shard only).

Now in `get_per_tensor_param`:
```python
params = self.module.state_dict()
params = convert_weight_keys(params, getattr(self.module, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.module))
...
per_tensor_param = (
    (
        name,
        param.to(device, non_blocking=True).full_tensor().to(torch.bfloat16, non_blocking=True)
        if isinstance(param, DTensor)
        else param,
    )
    for name, param in params.items()
)
```

The key: `ShardedTensor` is NOT `DTensor`. The `isinstance(param, DTensor)` check is False for `ShardedTensor`. So the ShardedTensor is passed through WITHOUT being gathered to a full tensor. 

The vLLM side receives ShardedTensor objects (which are local shards). The `weight.shape` in the bucketed transfer would be the LOCAL SHARD shape (e.g., half the parameter), not the full parameter shape. The vLLM server expects full parameter shapes.

But wait — can ShardedTensor even be serialized over ZMQ? Let me think...

The BucketedWeightSender does:
```python
self.buffer[offset : offset + weight.nbytes].copy_(weight.view(-1).view(torch.uint8), non_blocking=True)
```
